title: Variations Of Surfaces
notes: Open by framing the chapter as the surface analogue of the curve variation story. The point is not merely to move a surface, but to separate motions that change geometry from motions that only change labels, then read area and volume derivatives from local curvature data.

title: The Variational Question
notes: Use this slide to set the dependency chain for the lecture. Vector calculus on the surface supplies grad, div, and the rotation J. A one-parameter family supplies a velocity field. The first variation formula then says which scalar controls area in the normal direction.

title: Surface Calculus Is Metric Calculus
notes: Emphasize that the parameter rectangle is not the geometry. The induced metric converts a differential into a gradient, weights divergence by the area density, and defines the quarter-turn J in tangent planes. These choices make the formulas invariant under reparametrization.

title: Rotate A Gradient, Lose The Divergence
notes: The rotated-gradient identity is a useful calibration before variations begin. Locally, J grad g follows level curves of g, so its flow does not create or destroy area density in the interior. Boundary flux is still visible, which prepares the tangential part of the area formula.

title: Every Velocity Splits
notes: Present the decomposition as a measurement tool. The scalar phi is the signed normal speed that pushes the surface through space. The tangent field Z moves parameter labels along the surface. Only the normal part changes the embedded shape in the interior.

title: Tangential Motion Is Relabeling Until The Boundary
notes: Students often expect every visible arrow to change area. The important exception is that a tangential field with support in the interior is a reparametrization effect, while a tangential field crossing the boundary changes which patch is being measured through its boundary flux.

title: Area Density Has A Local Derivative
notes: This is the hinge formula for the chapter. The term 2 phi H is the normal response of area density, and div Z is the tangential transport term. Because the formula is local, integration can later convert the divergence term into a boundary contribution.

title: First Variation Of Area
notes: Move from the density identity to the integrated statement. With compact support away from the boundary, tangential divergence contributes no net area change, so the normal gradient of area is 2H N in this sign convention. With a boundary, the flux term must be kept.

title: Mean Curvature Sign Check
notes: The round sphere fixes the sign convention. With outward normal, the chapter uses H equal to one over R. If the sphere expands outward at constant speed, its area increases and its mean curvature decreases, giving a clean test for both first variation and curvature variation signs.

title: Curvature Also Varies
notes: Do not try to derive the full curvature-variation formula on the slide. Instead, identify the three kinds of terms: tangential transport of H, a Laplacian response to uneven normal speed, and a curvature-squared reaction. The sphere test checks the constant-speed case.

title: Minimal Surfaces
notes: Minimal means critical for area under compactly supported normal variations, not necessarily smallest among all competitors. Since arbitrary phi can probe every point, the first variation can vanish for all such tests only when H is zero everywhere on the surface.

title: Volume Adds One Constraint
notes: Here the cone-volume derivative supplies the constraint gradient. Its normal density is phi, while area has density 2H phi. The Lagrange multiplier equation can use a single constant multiplier only when H is constant on the surface.

title: Reading The Three Model Families
notes: Compare the models by what the Euler-Lagrange equation sees. Planes and Enneper-type patches represent H equal to zero. Round spheres represent positive constant H. A generic graph patch usually has H varying across the surface, so it fails the fixed-volume criticality test.

title: Notebook Diagnostics As Evidence
notes: Connect the lecture to the companion notebook without treating the figures as decoration. The checks measure divergence identities, variation-field reconstruction, finite-difference area derivatives, and sphere or minimal-surface calibrations. Each numerical residual is evidence for a formula in the slide chain.

title: A Safe Perturbation Lab
notes: Use this as an instructor prompt for experimentation. Changing phi tests the normal gradient of area. Changing Z tests the boundary flux. Changing the graph height tests whether the mean-curvature plot flattens toward a constant multiplier in the fixed-volume problem.

title: Recap: From Motion To Euler-Lagrange
notes: Close by repeating the dependency chain. Decompose the velocity, differentiate the area density, integrate and account for boundary flux, then read off criticality. The result is compact: unconstrained area gives H equal to zero, while fixed volume gives H constant.
